newsitem.title: USA: Yellen sees no sign of U.S. inflationary pressures.
newsitem.headline: Yellen sees no sign of U.S. inflationary pressures.

text.p: A top White House economic adviser, commenting on the June jobs figures, said on Thursday the U.S. economy remains on "solid footing" and there are no signs of inflationary pressures.

"Today's employment report confirms that the economy remains on solid footing: Unemployment hovers in a decades-low range, jobs are being created at a robust pace, and there are still no signs of inflationary pressures," Janet Yellen, who chairs the president's Council of Economic Advisers, said in a statement.

The Labor Department reported today that the unemployment rate rose to 5 percent in June from a 24-year low of 4.8 percent in May as private sector job growth slowed, particularly in several service industries.
It said 217,000 non-farm jobs were added to payrolls in June, up from 166,000 new jobs in May, but non-government job growth slowed to 151,000 from 180,000.

Noting that average hourly earnings rose 0.3 percent in June, Yellen said that over the past 12 months average hourly earnings have increased 3.5 percent, which she described as "a pace consistent with real wage gains for American workers, while inflation is still being held in check."
